{{Quote|Decades ago, the mercenary group known as The Mandalorians fractured, giving rise to a chaotic splinter group. They called themselves The 'Death Watch' and followed a barbarian called Vizsla, who believed that the Mandalorians should conquer the galaxy|[[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] describing The Death Watch to his [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]|<ref name="Open Seasons" />}}
The '''Death Watch'''—or '''''Kyr'tsad''''' in [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']]—was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] splinter group founded by [[Tor Vizsla]], who opposed [[Jaster Mereel]]'s [[Supercommando Codex]]. Their primary goal was to return the Mandalorians to their [[Mandalorian Crusaders|ancient roots]] as galactic crusaders, and advocated the savage raider mentality of past Mandalorians. The Death Watch fought Mereel's [[True Mandalorians]] for primacy during the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]], manipulating a team of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] into wiping them out at the [[Battle of Galidraan]]. When the only surviving True Mandalorian, [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], escaped from custody, he hunted and killed Tor Vizsla.

The Death Watch scattered and seemingly disbanded until the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] when they reemerged under the leadership of [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], targeting [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]] of the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]]. Striking from their [[Death Watch hideout|hidden base]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]], they orchestrated several [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] attacks on New Mandalorian cities and [[Kalevala/Legends|Kalevala]] while garnering support from the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Eventually, when they allied themselves with [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] and the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]], they successfully [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|took control]] of Mandalore from Duchess Kryze. Maul then killed Pre Vizsla, and the Death Watch splintered into two factions—those who gave their loyalty to Maul and those who refused to follow an outsider, led by [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan Kryze]]. When [[Spar]] founded the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] as Mandalore the Resurrector, the Death Watch went into hiding again, under the leadership of [[Lorka Gedyc]], but resurfaced again during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], operating out of a [[Death Watch bunker|base]] on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|They dressed themselves up as patriots wanting a return to the good old days of the Mando empire, but it was just a cover for organized crime.|[[Kal Skirata]]|<ref name="ImpCom501st" />}}
[[File:Vizsla.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Death Watch's founder, Tor Vizsla]]
In the wake of the [[Ithullan]] genocide in [[200 BBY/Legends|200 BBY]], many Mandalorian warriors expressed a desire to shed the dishonorable ways of the past.<ref name="HotM" /> A century and a half later, the charismatic warrior [[Jaster Mereel]] became the new [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], and instituted a new standard of Mandalorian behavior known as the [[Supercommando Codex]].<ref name="HotM" /> He asserted that the Mandalorians were simply highly-paid soldiers, and should conduct themselves as honorable mercenaries. However, not all agreed with the Codex and Mereel's radical changes. A barbaric soldier by the name of [[Tor Vizsla]] attracted warriors fond of the old ways into his own movement, giving birth to the Death Watch. The Death Watch were skilled warriors, but ill-disciplined to the extreme and plagued with constant in-fighting under the egotistical leadership of Vizsla.<ref name="HotM" /> In accordance with Vizsla's beliefs, the Death Watch stood for a return to the ways of the [[Mandalorian Crusaders|ancient Mandalorians]], raiders and savages, and aimed to eventually wage a second [[Mandalorian Wars|war of conquest]] across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Open Seasons" /> In turn, Mereel's faction recast themselves as the [[True Mandalorians]] and a [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|civil war]] broke out between the two groups.<ref name="Open Seasons" />

===Mandalorian Civil War===
{{Quote|It's the Death Watch!''"<br />"''Who?''"<br />"''Before your time, Silas. Ex-Mandalorians who split with Jaster years ago. We thought they were finished. Guess we were wrong.|[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] and [[Silas (Mandalorian)|Silas]] during an ambush by the Death Watch at the [[Battle of Korda Six]]|<ref name="JF:OS2">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 2]]</ref>}}
[[File:Deathwatch1.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The Death Watch]]
On the agricultural [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], the Death Watch [[Battle of Concord Dawn|engaged]] the True Mandalorians in a fierce firefight that ended in the True Mandalorians' retreat. As Jaster Mereel and his men fled into the farming fields, Vizsla ordered his own forces to hunt them down. When they came upon a young [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] working on his family's [[Harvester/Legends|harvester]], they took him captive and forced the boy to lead them to [[Fett homestead|his home]] where [[Fett (Elder Journeyman Protector)|Jango's father]] was harboring Mereel's troops.<ref name="Open Seasons" /> Vizsla savagely beat the man in front of Jango while he demanded the location of the hidden Mandalorians, going so far as threatening to shoot him in the head right in front of his son. However, [[Jango Fett's mother|Jango's mother]] intervened, killing one of the Death Watch soldiers with Vizla with a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]]. Jango was rescued from Vizsla by the intervention of Mereel and his soldiers, but his parents were murdered<ref name="Open Seasons" /> and [[Arla Fett|his sister]] taken by the Death Watch.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> As they escaped into the fields, Vizsla ordered that they be burned with the hopes of killing Mereel and the True Mandalorians.<ref name="Open Seasons" /> The Death Watch moved into a nearby town following their perceived victory over the True Mandalorians, intent on a celebratory raid before moving on to [[Moonus Mandel/Legends|Moonus Mandel]]. Unfortunately for them, the True Mandalorians were lying in wait, striking the Death Watch when their guard was down. Nearly all of the Death Watch soldiers fell to [[Blaster/Legends|blasterfire]] or perished in the bombing of their [[Death Watch tank|tank]], and although Jango Fett avenged the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his family by killing the Death Watch soldier responsible for their murders, Vizsla managed to escape.<ref name="Open Seasons" />

[[File:Battle_of_Korda_6.jpg|thumb|left|220px|The Death Watch [[Battle of Korda Six|ambushes]] [[True Mandalorians|The True Mandalorians]] on [[Korda Six]]]]
Years later, the Death Watch would lure their True Mandalorian foes into a [[Battle of Korda Six|trap]] on the planet [[Korda Six]]. When Jaster Mereel and his troops came to the aid of a [[Korda Defense Force]] security squad pinned down on the planet by local enemy forces, the Death Watch revealed themselves—much to the surprise of the True Mandalorians. Jango Fett, now a fully-fledged Mandalorian warrior, fought back dozens of Death Watch soldiers alongside the True Mandalorians under his command, while Jaster Mereel and his second-in-command [[Montross (bounty hunter)|Montross]] came under fire from Vizsla himself. Baring the scars from their previous encounter on his face, Vizsla rained down attacks from his four-wheeled tank on Montross and the injured Mereel. When Montross betrayed the wounded ''Mand'alor'' and left him alone on the battlefield, Vizsla was granted his revenge as he gunned down Mereel with his tank's [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]]. The True Mandalorians were forced to flee the planet and the Death Watch was victorious.<ref name="Open Seasons" />

[[File:Death_Watch_Might_Be_Evil_Guys.png|thumb|right|220px|The Death Watch plotting to destroy the Mandalorians]]
Approximately [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], the Death Watch became involved with [[Governor of Galidraan|the governor]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world [[Galidraan/Legends|Galidraan]]. The [[Governor/Legends|governor]] provided refuge for the Death Watch at his castle and was involved in funding Tor Vizsla's attempts to rebuild the Death Watch, presumably after a costly loss. He also hired the True Mandalorians to [[Battle of Galidraan|deal with]] an insurrection on his world as part of a plot by the Death Watch to draw in their enemy. While the True Mandalorians—now under the leadership of Jango Fett, replacing Jaster Mereel as ''Mand'alor''—dealt with the rebels, the Governor of Galidraan contacted the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], claiming that the that Mandalorians were murdering "political activists", along with women and children. In order to lend credence to these claims and gain the Jedi Council's assistance, Vizsla and his own troops provided the body count of innocents.<ref name="Open Seasons" /> Upon completing their contracted assignment, Jango Fett went to personally speak with Galidraan's governor, both to collect the Mandalorians' payment and to find out where Vizsla was being harbored. Vizsla and a few of his troops revealed themselves and opened fire on Fett, forcing him to escape out of a nearby window via [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] at the same time the [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|Jedi ships]] were arriving to deal with the supposed Mandalorian threat. Vizsla and the Death Watch had only to stand aside while the Jedi strike team under [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] all but wiped out the True Mandalorians, save for Fett himself who was captured and delivered into the custody of the governor of Galidraan who subsequently sold Fett into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]].<ref name="Open Seasons" />

[[File:Death_Rattle.png|thumb|left|220px|The Death Watch's flagship, [[Death Rattle|The Death Rattle]]]]
Two years later, Fett would escape and return to Galidraan, recovering his lost [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] and demanding the location of the Death Watch from the governor at blasterpoint. He would find the Death Watch forces aboard Vizsla's personal [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the ''[[Death Rattle]]'', over [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. Fett used a [[Jango Fett's starfighter|starfighter]] to cripple the ship's engines while assaulting the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], using his jetpack to fly through the [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]]. He clashed with Vizsla in a lengthy fight that spanned the halls of the dying ship and even into an escape pod, continuing on after crashing to the surface of Corellia. At the climax of their fight, both injured and Fett poisoned by Vizsla, a pack of [[dire-cat]]s attacked and killed Vizsla, while sparing the poisoned Fett. With Vizsla finally defeated, the remaining members of the group scattered throughout the galaxy,<ref name="Open Seasons" /> but although they were seemingly destroyed, the beliefs of the Death Watch remained amongst some Mandalorians.<ref name="O66" /><ref name="TMP" />

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Not everyone on Mandalore believes our commitment to peace is a sign of progress. There is a group that calls itself Death Watch. I imagine these are the renegades you are looking for. They idolize violence and the warrior ways of the past.|Duchess Satine Kryze of Mandalore to Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=DeathWatch-TMP.flac|<ref name="TMP" />}}
During the formation of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], Jango Fett—[[Clone template/Legends|clone template]] and primary military adviser for the Grand Army—hand-picked a group of one-hundred individuals, seventy-five of which were Mandalorian, to train elite [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] for the army, a group that would become known as the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]''—"Those Who No-Longer Exist".<ref name="Republic Commando: Hard Contact">''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''</ref> Two of the Mandalorian trainers, [[Isabet Reau]] and [[Dred Priest]], attempted to ingrain the beliefs of the Death Watch into their clones by secretly forming [[Battle Circle|battle circles]] in the bowels of [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]]. Jango Fett discovered the existence of the battle circles and quickly put them to an end, viciously beating Priest.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

[[File:DeathWatch-TCW.png|thumb|left|250px|The Death Watch at the time of the Clone Wars]]
Though weakened, the Death Watch managed to operate under the Mandalorian principle of ''ba'slan shev'la'', or "strategic disappearance".<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Maintaining a fairly secret existence following Tor Vizsla's death, the remains of the Death Watch showed themselves nearly twelve years later, shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]]. With the True Mandalorians gone and Jango Fett dead following the events on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], the Death Watch set its sights on the Mandalorian faction known as the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]], a reformist political faction emphasizing pacifism that was interested in moving the Mandalorians even further from its conquering warrior roots than the True Mandalorians, with their goal being a peaceful and neutral Mandalorian state. At the time, the Death Watch was operating from a [[Death Watch hideout|base]] on [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]], a [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], where they were secretly led by Concordia's governor, [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]].<ref name="TMP" /> In order to get support for their attempt at taking over the Mandalorian government, the Death Watch allied themselves with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. As part of this alliance, Death Watch [[Mandalorian Supercommando|commandos]] performed sabotage missions for the Separatists against [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] targets. One such mission involved a [[Unidentified Death Watch saboteur/Legends|commando]] attempting to sabotage a Republic [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]]; the Death Watch commando was captured, but rather than surrender and submit to questioning, he committed suicide.<ref name="TMP" /> His actions in addition to falsified rumors led to the Republic's belief that [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], leader of the New Mandalorians and head of the [[Council of Neutral Systems/Legends|Council of Neutral Systems]], was training a Mandalorian army for the Separatists.<ref name="TMP" />

[[File:PreVizsla-SWI115.png|thumb|right|175px|[[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], a Death Watch leader during the Clone Wars]]
In order to investigate this matter further, the Jedi Council dispatched [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to Mandalore to meet with Satine. At first, the Duchess and her advisers discounted any Mandalorian involvement until Kenobi showed holographic recordings of the Death Watch saboteur. She later revealed the existence of rumors of the Death Watch's return. This was later proven when a [[Death Watch bomber/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|bombed]] the [[Peace Park/Legends|memorial shrine]] in the New Mandalorian capital of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] before committing suicide when Kenobi attempted to apprehend him. Left at the bomb site was a holographic representation of the Death Watch symbol, further highlighting the group's return. During these events Pre Vizsla communicated with [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] who revealed his strategy for the Republic to establish peacekeeping forces on Mandalore. Dooku hoped this would cause unrest and lead the Mandalorian populace to the Death Watch's ideals. Kenobi later discovered the Death Watch base of operations on Concordia and Pre Vizsla revealed himself to the Jedi and the duchess as the leader of the faction. The Death Watch Mandalorians managed to escape and abandoned their base, allowing them to remain at large.<ref name="TMP" />

When Satine journeyed to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to dismiss any thought of [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|Republic occupation]], Death Watch made a [[Skirmish aboard the Coronet/Legends|second attempt on her life]]. Mandalore's senator, [[Tal Merrik/Legends|Tal Merrik]], was secretly in league with the Death Watch and used his senatorial stamp to smuggle several [[Assassin probe/Legends|assassin probes]] aboard the duchess' ship. When Kenobi gathered the senatorial passengers together and confronted them with a [[Probe killer/Legends|probe killer]], its docility betrayed Merrik and he made his move to take Kryze hostage. With the duchess in tow, he made his way to the bridge where he murdered the crew and contacted Vizsla for extraction. A trio of [[Droch-class boarding ship/Legends|''Droch''-class boarding ships]] attached themselves to the vessel and unloaded several [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] to cover Merrik's escape. When Kenobi attempted to arrest the senator, Merrik revealed that he had also taken the precaution of rigging the ship's engines to explode and made his way to the waiting boarding ships. Before he could make his escape, however, he was stabbed in the back by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="VoT">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref>

Once Satine safely arrived at the galactic capital, the Death Watch reoccupied their base on Concordia as a staging area for their impending invasion of Mandalore. A New Mandalorian scout reported to [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] of this development. Almec was confident that Death Watch could not take Mandalore without the citizens of Mandalore's support. During a holographic conference with Count Dooku, Pre Vizsla made his move to secure Mandalore's support. A Death Watch assassin was sent to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to assassinate Satine, as well as an informant who gave her a recording from Deputy Minister [[Jerec/Legends|Jerec]] pleading no military assistance. The assassin, however, failed to stop Satine from delivering the evidence to the Galactic Senate thanks to Kenobi's intervention. The Senate revoked its vote to dispatch Republic forces, which compelled Death Watch to cease its planned attack.<ref name="DoM">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref>

Death Watch then broke ties with Count [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and the Separatists and vowed to kill the Count. The Death Watch established a [[Death Watch camp|camp]] on the neutral planet of [[Carlac/Legends|Carlac]], kidnapping young females of the native [[Ming Po/Legends|Ming Po]]. At the same time, [[Lux Bonteri/Legends|Lux Bonteri]] chose to ally with Death Watch, believing them to be an honorable group, to kill Dooku, whom killed his [[Mina Bonteri/Legends|mother]], providing them with a holotrace to the Separatist leader's location. But at the same time, Ming Po chieftain, [[Pieter/Legends|Pieter]], demanded that Death Watch return their captives and leave the planet. At first, Vizsla seemed to comply to his demands, but then ordered his troops to burn down the Ming Po settlement, causing Bonteri to realize his error. However, one of Bonteri's companions was revealed to be a Jedi [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], who briefly fought off Death Watch before being captured. As Vizsla brought her back to their camp to execute her for her Order's crimes against Mandalore, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] rallied the Death Watch droids to rebel against their masters, creating a distraction for himself, Tano and Bonteri to escape.<ref name="AFIN">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref>

Sometime after Tano's and Bonteri's escape, the Republic followed a [[Crashed Munificent-class star frigate|Munificent-class star frigate]] to Carlac. They shot it down and went to the surface to finish off the surviving droids. They encountered Death Watch resistance, [[Camp Beskar|including]] [[Camp Kote|three]] [[Camp Ara'nov|camps]]. The Republic set up a [[Republic Outpost (Carlac)|outpost]] from where they could counter the Death Watch, and so the [[Skirmish on Carlac]] began. [[Unidentified Jedi Knight (Clone Wars)|A Jedi Knight]] joined the battle, destroying the three camps, killing [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Kellov]] and infiltrating a [[Unidentified captive village|village]] that the Death Watch held captive, threatening to destroy it if the Republic did not recall it's forces from the world. The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] infiltrated the village, however they were detected and the Death Watch started to burn it. The Republic dispatched a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] to douse the fires, although it raged on. The Jedi Knight defeated [[Kherr Dawar]], [[Kro Lann]], [[Mord Jayran]] and Vizsla himself, although he escaped.<ref name="CWA">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]</ref>

[[File:DeathWatchElite-Eminence.png|thumb|left|Four Death Watch members of high rank standing in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]]]
After the events on [[Carlac/Legends|Carlac]], Death Watch established a camp on the [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Zanbar/Legends|Zanbar]] in order to rebuild when they discovered the escape pod of [[Darth Maul/Legends|Maul]] and his brother [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage]], who had laid claim to the titles of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] and were wounded by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. An alliance would be forged from this action as the lives of Maul and Savage were spared by Death Watch and with them began to build an army of crime lords and gangsters known as the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]] to help with a [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|coup]] to overthrow the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]].<ref name="E">{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}}</ref> As the plan progressed, the Shadow Collective's gang and crime lord members attacked various targets in [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] as they fought against the New Mandalorian police forces and overwhelming them with numbers. Once the people were rioting for the government's response and actions during the crisis, [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan]], and several other members of Death Watch appeared. [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], the current Duchess of Mandalore, accused them of having some involvement with the attacks, but she was ignored as the people rallied for battle against the Shadow Collective. Death Watch moved quickly and effectively against the crime lords and captured them and Savage, before heading to the royal palace and arresting Maul, along with Satine.
Vizsla declared himself the new leader of Mandalore, and promised that he would return the Mandalorians to their warrior heritage.

Maul and Savage soon escaped, and Maul challenged Pre Vizsla to a duel for the title of [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] and control of Death Watch. As the two fought, Pre was at first able to hold his own against the Sith Lord but eventually began to tire. After pushing him to the ground, Maul used Vizsla's own [[Darksaber/Legends|Darksaber]] to [[Sai cha/Legends|behead]] him and take control of both the planet and Death Watch. However, a single squad known as the [[Nite Owls/Legends|Nite Owls]], led by Pre Vizsla's most trusted lieutenant, Bo-Katan, refused to acknowledge Maul as Mandalore, calling those who did traitors. Maul ordered them executed, but they were able to escape, killing several of Maul's loyalists in the ensuing firefight.<ref name="SoR">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref> Effectively, Death Watch was split in two—those who swore fealty to Maul, known as [[Mandalorian super commando/Legends|Mandalorian super commandos]], painted their armor red, while those who followed Bo-Katan retained their blue color scheme.<ref name="The Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref>

The Nite Owls, aided by Satine's loyalists, included her nephew [[Korkie Kryze/Legends|Korkie]], attempted to spring the Duchess from prison and got her outside Sundari where she could send a message to [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] before she was recaptured. As the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] refused to intervene in what they perceived to be an internal Mandalorian affair, Kenobi was forced to come alone. After a failed rescue attempt, in which Maul executed Satine, the Nite Owls helped Kenobi escape and [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|fought]] against the Maul loyalists to allow Kenobi to depart Mandalore and warn the Republic about the truth of its downfall. However, Maul was subsequently defeated and nearly killed by his former Sith Master, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="The Lawless" />

When the [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC trooper]] deserter known as [[Spar]] fled Kamino and journeyed to Mandalore, where he eventually took up the role of "Mandalore the Resurrector", he invited many former Death Watch members to join his army of [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]].<ref name="HotM" /> Although Spar formed the Protectors in the image of the True Mandalorians,<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> the Death Watch's desire for Mandalore's return to its warrior roots would come to fruition when the Protectors overturned Mandalore's status as a neutral [[Star system/Legends|system]] and aligned with the Confederacy of Independent Systems.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

===Galactic Civil War and decline===
{{Quote|We conquered whole star systems. We had an empire. When cities heard our armies were coming, populations fled before a shot was fired. Now we cling to a pathetic sector of dirtball planets, we scramble for the crumbs that the cowardly ''aruetiise'' throw when they want us to fight for them, and they use us as a breeding stock for their clone armies. The ''aruetiise'' will always treat us like an animal species to be used for their convenience until we stand up for ourselves again.|Lorka Gedyc|<ref name="ImpCom501st" />}}
[[File:Fenri_Dalso.jpg|thumb|left|140px|[[Fenri Dalso]], a Death Watch member during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]]]
By the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Declaration of a New Order|foundation]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Lorka Gedyc]] had become the leader of the Death Watch as it continued to exist in hiding. Among this latest generation of Death Watch were former ''Cuy'val Dar'' members Isabet Reau and Dred Priest.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> During a run in with fellow former ''Cuy'val Dar'' [[Mij Gilamar]] in the Mandalorian capital [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], Priest revealed that the Death Watch was indeed still in existence—even openly wearing the group's sigil on his shoulder plate, albeit in a dark blue coloration—and that Lorka Gedyc had "big plans" for the future. He also believed that the Death Watch had changed under Gedyc and was different than the way it had been under Vizsla. The Death Watch had also allied with the Empire, with Priest even assisting the Imperials move in to [[City of Bone|the garrison]] being established outside Keldabe. When he'd learned all he felt he could, Gilamar surprise-attacked Priest, stabbing and killing him, and threw his body in the [[Kelita River]], firmly believing that the Death Watch's return to prominence couldn't be allowed for the good of the Mandalorians.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

By [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]], [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] had come into conflict with the Death Watch. The [[Fromm Gang/Legends|Fromm Gang]] offered the service of their [[Annoo-dat Blue|Annoo-dat]] [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] to help Jabba deal with this threat.<ref name="TDRA2">{{SW|url=news/the-droids-re-animated-part-2|series=The Droids Re-Animated|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

By the year [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> with Mandalore now firmly under the control of the Galactic Empire,<ref name="TEA" /> a remnant of the Death Watch had fled to the [[Tree/Legends|forested]] moon of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. Operating out of a hidden [[Death Watch bunker|underground bunker]], they were led by a [[Unidentified Death Watch Overlord|Human male Mandalorian]] who made use of the [[overlord]] title. From the bunker, the Overlord commanded a force of Death Watch [[Wraith (Death Watch)|Wraiths]], [[Ghost (Death Watch)|Ghosts]], and [[Bloodguard]]s,<ref name="swg" /> while rekindling Death Watch's relationship with Black Sun during the Clone Wars,<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> contracting with the syndicate's [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] in exchange for their aid in furthering Death Watch goals.<ref name="swg" /> In the meantime, another Death Watch overlord, the [[Black UnNamed]], commanded a force of Death Watch starfighters, including [[Kihraxz assault fighter]]s, [[Ixiyen-class fast attack craft|''Ixiyen''-class fast attack crafts]] and [[Rihkxyrk assault fighter]]s, in the [[Red Sin Chimaera]] quadrant of the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]].<ref name="SWG:Es">{{SWGcite|exp=JtL|type=other|Endor system}}</ref>

[[File:DeathWatchOverlord.png|thumb|right|175px|The Death Watch Overlord on Endor]]
Though Death Watch had fallen into obscurity, word of their survival on Endor eventually reached Imperial [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[D'krn]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], who believed that the Death Watch bunker's overlord could be a promising [[Clone template/Legends|candidate]] for a new wave of [[Clone stormtrooper|cloned stormtroopers]],<ref name="swg" /> just as Jango Fett had been for the former Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]].<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> To that end, D'krn hired a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] to retrieve a sample of the Overlord's [[Blood/Legends|blood]]. The survival of Death Watch on Endor had also come to the attention of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who was working for [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] on Tatooine at the time. As the son of Jango Fett—who had fought Death Watch to their near eradication decades earlier—Boba Fett sought to see the splinter group dealt with once and for all, offering assistance in breaching the bunker and payment to the spacers if they eliminated the rogue Mandalorians. The spacers eventually assaulted the Endor bunker, killing numerous Death Watch troops including their overlord, before returning to D'krn with a vial of his blood.<ref name="swg" />

In the early days of the Rebellion, a man wearing armor similar to that of a Death Watch soldier was seen protecting [[Tungo Li]] during the hearing of [[Janek Sunber/Legends|Janek Sunber]].<ref name="MBME">''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: My Brother, My Enemy]]''</ref>

===Legacy===
The Death Watch was far from loved in the eyes of many Mandalorians. To most, they were considered little more than savages,<ref name="Open Seasons" /> hooligans,<ref name="TMP" /> and undisciplined thugs rather than soldiers.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Following the outbreak of the Mandalorian Civil War, Jango Fett considered the Death Watch to be "ex-Mandalorians" due to their radical beliefs and refusal to [[Resol'nare|follow the ''Mand'alor'']].<ref name="Open Seasons" /> The New Mandalorian government labeled them as terrorists and vandals for their destructive actions in opposing the government's peaceful ways.<ref name="TMP" /> Walon Vau, a member of the ''Cuy'val Dar'', was known to say the Death Watch was the only group he truly considered his enemy.<ref name="O66" /> [[Kal Skirata]], another ''Cuy'val Dar'' member, felt that the Death Watch—at least its incarnation under Tor Vizsla—was more interested in theft and other crime rather than their supposed goals of reinstating a Mandalorian empire.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

In combination with the armor worn by the [[Thyrsian]] [[Sun Guard]], Death Watch armor served as a partial inspiration for that of the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Royal Guard]], taking advantage of the group's ferocious reputation.<ref name="ImpSB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

As a child growing up on [[Plavin 6]], [[Nashiak Llalik]] was fascinated with the armor worn by the Death Watch. He read a lot about them and entertained his younger sister, [[Saren Llalik|Saren]], with stories about their armor. As an adult, Saren regretted being separated from her brother, partly because she would have enjoyed hearing those stories again.<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

By [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], ''Mand'alor'' [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] stated in a conversation with [[Jaing Skirata]] that the destruction of the Death Watch was his father's lasting legacy for the Mandalorians.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

==Symbol==
[[File:DeathWatchSymbol-SWcom.png|thumb|right|100px|The revised Death Watch symbol during the Clone Wars]]
The sign of the Death Watch was the symbol of Clan Vizsla,<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> which was designed after a stylized [[Shriek-hawk/Legends|''jai'galaar'']] in mid-dive, colored [[Color/Legends|red]]. By the Clone Wars and after, however, the symbol's color had been changed to blue.<ref name="TMP" /><ref name="ImpCom501st" />
